newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Otter June qtr gold production up 42 pct.
newsitem.headline: Otter June qtr gold production up 42 pct.

text.p: Otter Gold Mines Ltd on Tuesday reported a 42 percent rise in its net gold production in the June quarter to 31,323 ounces.
Net gold production was 106,167 ounces for the 1996/97 year, the company said.
Otter said the June quarter was both productive and profitable for the Tanami Mine northwest of Alice Springs in Australia.
"The production rate more than compensated for the shortfall experienced in the March quarter caused by wet season delays," the company said.

A total of 40,857 ounces of gold was produced in Tanami in the quarter, at an operating cost of NZ$366 per ounce. Otter is manager of the Tanami joint venture with a 60 percent equity stake. Acacia Resources Ltd holds 40 percent.
"The Tanami Mine is now established as one of Australia's lower cost gold producers with a record 131,532 ounces recorded for the 1996/97 year," Otter said.
Tanami ore reserves rose by 19 percent to 521,000 ounces. Otter said it had located "significant" mineralisation at Galifrey, 25 kilometres south of the Tanami Mine.
It had applied for permits to allow operations at Martha Hill to be expanded to 2007.

The company said its Beaconsfield feasibility study was close to completion, with a probable ore reserve of 1.534 million tonnes at 22.3 g/t, giving 1.1 million ounces (Otter's share 280,000 ounces via Allstate Explorations NL).

Otter said its net equity reserves totalled 708,000 ounces of gold and 1.1 million ounces of silver, while its resources totalled 1.3 million ounces of gold and 3.2 million ounces of silver, including reserves.
